import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Infinitude of Wall–Sun–Sun primes

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall%E2%80%93Sun%E2%80%93Sun_prime)
-/

open Algebra (IsQuadraticExtension)
open NumberField

namespace QuadraticAlgebra
variable {d : ℤ} [Fact <| Squarefree d] [Fact <| d ≠ 1]

/-- The discriminant of `ℚ[√d]` for `d ≥ 2` squarefree congruent to 1 mod 4 is `d`. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11, simp]
lemma discr_rat_of_modEq_one (hd₄ : d ≡ 1 [ZMOD 4]) : discr (QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0) = d := by
  sorry

/-- The discriminant of `ℚ[√d]` for `d ≥ 2` squarefree not congruent to 1 mod 4 is `4 * d`. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11, simp]
lemma discr_rat_of_not_modEq_one (hd₄ : ¬ d ≡ 1 [ZMOD 4]) :
    discr (QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0) = 4 * d := by
  sorry

end QuadraticAlgebra

namespace Algebra
variable {K L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]

variable (K L) in
/-- A quadratic algebra `L` over a field `K` is isomorphic to the explicit quadratic algebra
`QuadraticAlgebra K a b` for some `a b : K`. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
lemma exists_quadraticAlgebra_of_isQuadraticExtension [IsQuadraticExtension K L] :
    ∃ a b, Nonempty (L ≃ₐ[K] QuadraticAlgebra K a b) := by
  sorry

/-- An algebra `L` is quadratic over a field `K` iff it is isomorphic to the explicit quadratic
algebra `QuadraticAlgebra K a b` for some `a b : K`. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
lemma isQuadraticExtension_iff_exists_quadraticAlgebra :
    IsQuadraticExtension K L ↔ ∃ a b, Nonempty (L ≃ₐ[K] QuadraticAlgebra K a b) where
  mp _ := exists_quadraticAlgebra_of_isQuadraticExtension ..
  mpr := by rintro ⟨a, b, ⟨e⟩⟩; sorry

end Algebra

namespace NumberField
variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]

variable (K) in
/-- A quadratic number field `K` is isomorphic to the explicit quadratic field
`QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0` for some squarefree `d : ℤ` not equal to 1. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
lemma exists_quadraticAlgebra_of_isQuadraticExtension [IsQuadraticExtension ℚ K] :
    ∃ d ≠ (1 : ℤ), Squarefree d ∧ Nonempty (K ≃+* QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0) := by
  sorry

/-- A number field `K` is quadratic iff it is isomorphic to the explicit quadratic field
`QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0` for some squarefree `d : ℤ` not equal to 1. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
lemma isQuadraticExtension_iff_exists_quadraticAlgebra :
    IsQuadraticExtension ℚ K ↔
      ∃ d ≠ (1 : ℤ), Squarefree d ∧ Nonempty (K ≃+* QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0) where
  mp _ := exists_quadraticAlgebra_of_isQuadraticExtension _
  mpr := by rintro ⟨d, hd₁, hd, ⟨e⟩⟩; sorry

/-- An integer `D` is a fundamental discriminant iff it is the discriminant of the explicit
quadratic field `QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0` for some squarefree `d : ℤ` not equal to 1. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
lemma isFundamentalDiscr_iff_exists_discr_quadraticAlgebra {D : ℤ} :
    IsFundamentalDiscr D ↔ ∃ (d : ℤ) (_ : Fact <| d ≠ 1) (_ : Fact <| Squarefree d),
      discr (QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0) = D where
  mp := by
    rintro (⟨⟨d, rfl⟩, hD₄, hD⟩ | ⟨hD₁, hD₄, hD⟩)
    · simp only [ne_eq, OfNat.ofNat_ne_zero, not_false_eq_true, mul_div_cancel_left₀] at hD hD₄
      have : Fact <| d ≠ 1 := ⟨by rintro rfl; simp at hD₄⟩
      have : Fact <| Squarefree d := ⟨hD⟩
      exact ⟨d, inferInstance, inferInstance, QuadraticAlgebra.discr_rat_of_not_modEq_one hD₄⟩
    · have : Fact <| D ≠ 1 := ⟨hD₁⟩
      have : Fact <| Squarefree D := ⟨hD⟩
      exact ⟨D, inferInstance, inferInstance, QuadraticAlgebra.discr_rat_of_modEq_one hD₄⟩
  mpr := by
    rintro ⟨d, _, _, rfl⟩; by_cases hd₄ : d ≡ 1 [ZMOD 4] <;> simp [*, IsFundamentalDiscr, Fact.out]

/-- An integer `D` is a fundamental discriminant iff it is the discriminant of some number field. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
lemma isFundamentalDiscr_iff_exists_discr_numberField {D : ℤ} :
    IsFundamentalDiscr D ↔
      ∃ (K : Type) (_ : Field K) (_ : NumberField K), IsQuadraticExtension ℚ K ∧ discr K = D := by
  rw [isFundamentalDiscr_iff_exists_discr_quadraticAlgebra]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨d, _, _, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨_, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance, rfl⟩
  · rintro ⟨K, _, _, _, rfl⟩
    obtain ⟨d, hd₁, hd, ⟨e⟩⟩ := exists_quadraticAlgebra_of_isQuadraticExtension K
    have : Fact <| d ≠ 1 := ⟨hd₁⟩
    have : Fact <| Squarefree d := ⟨hd⟩
    exact ⟨d, inferInstance, inferInstance, discr_eq_discr_of_ringEquiv _ e.symm⟩

end NumberField

namespace WallSunSun

/--
A prime $p$ is a Wall–Sun–Sun prime if and only if $L_p \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$, where $L_p$ is the
$p$-th Lucas number. It is conjectured that there is at least one Wall–Sun–Sun prime.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem exists_isWallSunSunPrime : ∃ p, IsWallSunSunPrime p := by
  sorry

/--
A prime $p$ is a Wall–Sun–Sun prime if and only if $L_p \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$, where $L_p$ is the
$p$-th Lucas number. It is conjectured that there are infinitely many Wall-Sun-Sun primes.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinite_isWallSunSunPrime : {p : ℕ | IsWallSunSunPrime p}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
A Lucas–Wieferich prime associated with $(a,b)$ is an odd prime $p$, not dividing $a^2 - 4b$, such
that $U_{p-\varepsilon}(a,b) \equiv 0 \pmod{p^2}$ where $U(a,b)$ is the Lucas sequence of the first
kind and $\varepsilon$ is the Legendre symbol $\left({\tfrac {a^2-4b}{p}}\right)$.
The discriminant of this number is the quantity $a^2 - 4b$. It is conjectured that there are
infinitely many Lucas–Wieferich primes of any given non-one fundamental discriminant.

TODO: Source this conjecture
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinite_isWallSunSunPrime_of_disc_eq {D : ℤ} (hD : IsFundamentalDiscr D)
    (hD₁ : D ≠ 1) :
    {p : ℕ | ∃ a b, a ^ 2 - 4 * b = D ∧ IsLucasWieferichPrime a b p}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end WallSunSun

findings.description: The existentially quantified Lucas parameters may vary with p, so this does not describe Wall–Sun–Sun primes of a fixed discriminant in the source's sense. In fact, for every fundamental D, the displayed set equals {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ Odd p ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ D}; I proved this equality and the entire claimed infinitude independently in Lean, without sorry. For example, when D = 5, any odd prime p ≠ 5 qualifies by choosing a = p² and b = (p⁴ − 5)/4: the index p − (5/p) is even, and U at an even index is divisible by a. In particular, p = 3 qualifies with (a,b) = (9,19), since U₄(9,19) = 387 is divisible by 9. But 3 is not a conventional Wall–Sun–Sun prime: L₃ = 4 is not congruent to 1 modulo 9.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall%E2%80%93Sun%E2%80%93Sun_prime#Wall%E2%80%93Sun%E2%80%93Sun_primes_with_discriminant_D, identifies D = 5 with conventional Wall–Sun–Sun primes and conjectures infinitude for every fundamental discriminant D ≠ 1. Its cited reference, Elsenhans–Jahnel, The Fibonacci sequence modulo p², arXiv:1006.0824, Remark 2.2.8 (LaTeX read at https://arxiv.org/e-print/1006.0824), defines the real-quadratic-field generalization using a fundamental unit ε of the fixed field: ε^(p−1) ≡ 1 modulo p² in the split case and ε^(2p+2) ≡ 1 in the inert case, not arbitrary Lucas parameters chosen for each prime.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the existential Lucas-parameter condition by a sourced definition of Wall–Sun–Sun primes for the fixed quadratic field/discriminant. For the real-quadratic version in Elsenhans–Jahnel, use the congruences for a fundamental unit of that field; clarify the intended definition for negative discriminants if retaining them. The corrected D = 5 predicate should specialize to IsWallSunSunPrime. Merely moving unrestricted ∃ a b outside the infinitude assertion is insufficient, since degenerate fixed choices such as a = 0 also give trivial examples.

findings.description: The docstring says 'the discriminant of some number field', whereas the formal statement correctly requires a quadratic number field through IsQuadraticExtension ℚ K. The omitted qualification matters: with this file's definition, IsFundamentalDiscr 1 is false although ℚ is a number field with discriminant 1. The Lean theorem itself is correct.
findings.source_evidence: The docstring is at WallSunSun.lean:102. Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadratic_field#Discriminant, states that discriminants of quadratic fields are exactly the fundamental discriminants apart from 1. The linked fundamental-discriminant article gives the same quadratic-field characterization.
findings.suggested_fix: Change 'some number field' to 'some quadratic number field', retaining the existing Lean statement and its nontrivial-discriminant convention.

reformulations.difference: The predicate uses the Lucas-number congruence L_p ≡ 1 modulo p² rather than the Fibonacci/Pisano-period definition.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Wikipedia's Equivalent definitions section explicitly identifies these conditions for primes, as does MathWorld. LucasSequence.V 1 (-1) has precisely the standard Lucas initial values and recurrence. The small exceptional primes do not introduce extra witnesses: Lean checks show that 2, 3, and 5 fail the Lucas congruence, while 0 and 1 fail primality. Thus the existential statement is the source's existence conjecture.

reformulations.difference: Infinitude is stated using the Lucas-number characterization rather than the Fibonacci/Pisano-period characterization.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The prime predicates are pointwise equivalent by the equivalent definitions explicitly recorded in Wikipedia and MathWorld, so their sets of primes, and hence their infinitude assertions, coincide.

reformulations.difference: This supporting definition excludes 1, whereas Wikipedia includes 1 among fundamental discriminants. Its divisible-by-four branch also uses 'not congruent to 1' instead of 'congruent to 2 or 3'.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: I proved IsFundamentalDiscr D ↔ (the Wikipedia arithmetic definition for D ∧ D ≠ 1). Squarefreeness excludes the remaining residue 0 modulo 4 in the divisible-by-four branch. The conjecture explicitly assumes D ≠ 1 already, so the domain is unchanged. The auxiliary field-discriminant equivalences use precisely the corresponding nontrivial convention: fundamental discriminants other than 1 are the quadratic-field discriminants.

reformulations.difference: The classification uses a ring equivalence K ≃+* QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0 rather than explicitly requiring an equivalence of ℚ-algebras.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every unital ring equivalence between ℚ-algebras preserves rational scalars. I proved Nonempty (K ≃+* L) ↔ Nonempty (K ≃ₐ[ℚ] L) using RingEquiv.toRatAlgEquiv and the forgetful map. Thus the ring-equivalence formulation, also used by the preceding existence lemma, loses no extension-field compatibility.

review.notes: Checked all 11 declarations. The classical existence and infinitude problems remain open in the consulted source; the elementary proof of the discriminant variant diagnoses its statement, not a solution of the source problem. The remaining auxiliary mathematical statements are sound. Negative squarefree d are valid in the signed discriminant formulas, so no positivity hypothesis should be added merely because the two docstrings mention d ≥ 2. Jacobi equals Legendre at the admitted prime denominators, and the integer index before toNat is at least 2, so neither symbol defaults nor truncation cause an additional defect. Final experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, which compiles successfully. In particular, Review.declared_set_eq_odd_unramified_primes and Review.declared_discriminant_claim_is_elementary have no sorryAx dependency; their only axioms are propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The reviewed file's hash still matches the committed file.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.WallSunSun

/-! A concrete discrepancy in the discriminant-generalized Wall–Sun–Sun conjecture. -/

-- WallSunSun.infinite_isWallSunSunPrime_of_disc_eq:
-- At the admissible discriminant D = 5, its set contains 3 via (a,b) = (9,19),
-- although the source's D = 5 case is the classical one, which rejects 3.
example : NumberField.IsFundamentalDiscr (5 : ℤ) ∧ (5 : ℤ) ≠ 1 ∧
    3 ∈ {p : ℕ | ∃ a b, a ^ 2 - 4 * b = (5 : ℤ) ∧ IsLucasWieferichPrime a b p} ∧
    ¬ IsWallSunSunPrime 3 := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num [NumberField.IsFundamentalDiscr, Int.ModEq],
    by norm_num, ⟨9, 19, by norm_num, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · refine ⟨by norm_num, by decide, by norm_num, ?_⟩
    norm_num [jacobiSym, Int.ModEq]
    change 9 ∣ LucasSequence.U 9 19 4
    norm_num [LucasSequence.U] -- U₄(9,19) = 387 = 9 · 43.
  · intro h
    have hm := h.lucasNumber_modeq
    norm_num [lucasNumber, LucasSequence.V, Int.ModEq] at hm -- L₃ = 4 ≢ 1 (mod 9).

submission.summary: Replaced the prime-dependent Lucas parameters with a fixed real quadratic field and a fundamental unit, using the source’s split/inert congruences in its ring of integers. Explicitly restricted the generalization to the sourced real-quadratic case, rather than inventing a negative-discriminant definition, and added the Elsenhans–Jahnel reference. Also corrected the minor docstring omission of “quadratic.” Compilation reports only expected `sorry` warnings; separate congruence sanity checks pass.

open scoped NumberTheorySymbols in
/--
Let $K$ be a real quadratic number field with discriminant $D$ and fundamental unit $\varepsilon$,
so every unit of $\mathcal O_K$ is of the form $\pm\varepsilon^n$ for some $n\in\mathbb Z$.
It is conjectured that there are infinitely many odd primes $p\nmid D$ such that
$\varepsilon^{p-1}\equiv 1\pmod{p^2}$ when $\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)=1$, and
$\varepsilon^{2p+2}\equiv 1\pmod{p^2}$ when $\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)=-1$.
The congruences are taken in $\mathcal O_K/(p^2)$.

This is the real-quadratic case of the discriminant generalization in Wikipedia, using the
notion of an exceptional prime from Elsenhans–Jahnel, Remark 2.2.8. For $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt 5)$,
one may take $\varepsilon=(1+\sqrt 5)/2$, giving the classical Wall–Sun–Sun primes.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinite_isWallSunSunPrime_of_disc_eq {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]
    [IsQuadraticExtension ℚ K] [IsTotallyReal K] {D : ℤ} (hD : discr K = D)
    (ε : (𝓞 K)ˣ) (hε : ∀ u : (𝓞 K)ˣ, ∃ n : ℤ, u = ε ^ n ∨ u = -(ε ^ n)) :
    {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ Odd p ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ D ∧
      (p : 𝓞 K) ^ 2 ∣ (ε : 𝓞 K) ^ (if J(D | p) = 1 then p - 1 else 2 * p + 2) - 1}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end WallSunSun
